Subject: Dedicated capacity recap & next steps — Acme Health

Hi Sana / Tom,

Thanks again for the time today — it was helpful to walk through Acme's short- and medium-term inference needs. Below is a concise recap of what we heard, the proposed dedicated configuration, and next steps. Please flag anything I missed.

Summary of pain points:
- High variance in peak traffic causing unpredictable latency for production scoring pipelines (esp. 99th percentile).
- Need for strict data isolation (PHI/PII) and VPC-only access for models.
- Desire to control model versions and pin to specific quantization profiles for consistency.
- Procurement/security will require SOC 2 excerpts and a clear SLA for uptime and support.

Goals you stated:
- Guaranteed capacity for production (reserved GPUs) to remove tail latency spikes.
- Private networking / VPC and audit logging for compliance.
- Predictable economics with the ability to burst when needed.

Proposed dedicated capacity (initial):
- Reserved pool: 8 A100-equivalent GPUs (we can translate to specific instance types by region).
- Burst capacity: autoscale to 12 GPUs for short bursts (minutes-hours).
- Deployment: Private (VPC) Dedicated with customer-managed networking; full KV-cache persistence and per-token billing.
- Target SLA: baseline 99.9% (we can discuss 99.95% for enterprise term).
- Pilot: 3-week pilot to validate latency, throughput, and integration patterns.

Action items / next steps:
1) I will send the dedicated proposal and SOC 2 excerpt attached for procurement/security review. (attached: redwood_dedicated_proposal_ACME_20260318.pdf, SOC2-excerpt.pdf)
2) Please confirm expected peak concurrent requests and average sequence lengths so we can finalize sizing.
3) If procurement confirms, we’ll schedule a technical deep-dive with Rishi to lock in autoscaling and network setup.
4) Tentative timeline: procurement + security sign-off (1-2 weeks), provision reserved pool (2-4 weeks depending on region), start 3-week pilot.

Thanks — I’ll follow up with a slightly more detailed sizing proposal once I have the peak traffic numbers.

Best,

Thanks Marissa — this is a great recap. A few clarifications from our side after chatting with Tom and looping procurement: 

1) Isolation & networking: the VPC/private deployment is a hard requirement. We cannot allow egress to public endpoints from the inference layer. Will Redwood provide a customer-managed subnet with private IPs?
2) SLA: our security/compliance team is pushing for 99.95% for critical scoring pipelines. Is that something you can offer for Dedicated with the right contract terms?
3) Autoscaling & burst: how quickly can you provision burst capacity? Our traffic can spike by ~40-60% for 20-90 minutes during business hours, and we need bursts to come up within <10 minutes ideally.
4) Lead time & cost: procurement needs an estimate for lead time to provision reserved GPUs and a ballpark monthly committed cost (we can refine after sizing).
5) Data residency: all data and logs must reside in the us-west-2 region. Confirm you can pin the dedicated pool to that region.

CC'ing procurement for visibility. Procurement, can you confirm the vendor onboarding doc we need to start?

Thanks Sana — great questions. Quick answers below and next steps. Replying with Rishi and Vivek on cc to help with sizing and contracting.

1) Isolation & networking: yes — we will provision a dedicated VPC-only deployment for Acme and we support customer-managed subnets and private IPs. No public egress by default; egress can be locked down per company policy.

2) SLA: Dedicated customers can request an elevated SLA. Standard Dedicated SLA is 99.9%; we can discuss 99.95% as an enterprise addendum (typically tied to capacity commits and a premium). I'll loop legal with the draft SLO language.

3) Autoscaling & burst lead times: for the proposed pool we can autoscale within ~5-10 minutes for short bursts via our smart routing and warm standby capacity. If you need sub-2-minute scale-up we should discuss a higher baseline or pinned burst capacity.

4) Lead time & cost: provisioning a reserved pool in us-west-2 is usually 2-4 weeks (inventory dependent). Ballpark monthly committed cost for an 8 A100-equivalent pool with burst to 12 would be in the range of $XXk–$YYk/month — Rishi, can you provide a tighter estimate based on our current pricing bands?

5) Data residency: we will pin the cluster to us-west-2 and ensure logs are stored in your region.

Attachments: updated proposal with pricing band (redwood_dedicated_proposal_ACME_updated_20260319.pdf) and SOC 2 excerpt (SOC2-excerpt.pdf).

Next steps / owner
- Sana: confirm expected peak concurrent requests / typical seq lengths (by end of week).
- Procurement: start vendor onboarding and share any mandatory forms.
- Rishi: prepare a detailed sizing + cost estimate.
- Vivek: draft SOW + contract starter and surface any standard redlines.

Once procurement signs off we’ll book a provisioning window. Happy to jump on a call with procurement/security if that helps.
